objectClass.notes: The rack must remain visibly open. Dense bundles may overlap, but they cannot collapse into one foliage wall that hides rods, jars and shelf depth.

reasoning: The frame itself is simple, but the identity depends on many separated small organic bundles and pharmacy tools.
Three hanging rows, multiple herb palettes, garlic, jars and roof tiles create high repetition and occlusion density.
The rack needs independent front and narrow-side review to prove it is open and structurally braced.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Complex depth is required by the organic bundle variation, tile assembly and multi-material apothecary tool shelf.

unknownsToResolveBeforeImplementation: Plant species are stylized into five readable leaf/flower families instead of botanical simulation.
The tile canopy uses repeated curved shells rather than a baked roof mesh.

details.description: Four slender oak posts rise from iron shoes on individual limestone feet.
Front and rear lintels, side rails and four diagonal braces keep the open frame rigid.
Eighty-eight curved terracotta field tiles overlap on two slopes.
Eleven half-round ridge tiles cap a projected oak ridge beam.
Three black iron rods span the front plane and terminate in side eyes.
Sixteen separated bundles hang from individual rope loops and knots.
Each bundle carries curved stems and alternating dimensional leaves in several dry-green palettes.
Lavender, rose and chamomile-like petal clusters interrupt the foliage rows.
Two pale garlic bundles use lobed bulbs and separate stems.
Two open plank shelves and side rails preserve visible depth beneath the bundles.
Five individually shaped and colored ceramic jars carry corks, raised rims, parchment labels and ink marks.
A brass mortar with raised rim and angled pestle occupies the upper shelf.
Five irregular folded parchment leaves are bound by a twine loop.
A tapered wicker basket uses four woven rings, fourteen ribs and an arched handle.
Projected pruning shears hang opposite a stitched leather pouch with flap and brass clasp.

anatomy.note: Object domain; character anatomy is not applicable.

definitionOfDone: The rack reads as an open, weather-protected drying station with separated plant bundles and a recognizable apothecary shelf in main and narrow-side views.

qualityCriteria: Posts, braces, rods and shelf depth remain visible through the contents.
Bundles separate into stems, leaves, flowers, garlic and bindings.
Jars, mortar, parchment, basket, shears and pouch read as distinct tools.
Oak, clay, iron, plants, ceramic, brass, cork, parchment, wicker and leather respond independently.

antiShallowSpecRules: No flat foliage curtain may pass.
The canopy may not be one orange slab.
Jars and tools may not be painted onto the shelf.
